Strait of Hormuz Status: October 10, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
10 October 2026 .
Brent $ 104.72 + 0.83 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 Azernews.az reports 11 commercial ships have been attacked in and around the Strait of Hormuz since early October; no major wire in this feed carries this figure.

02 The Maritime Executive reports the IRGC has expanded its threat against non-compliant vessels as more tankers are struck.

03 CNBC reports tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz have surged to a wartime high as Iran seeks to choke off oil exports.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to normal commercial traffic, with IMF PortWatch recording 4 transits on October 4 against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Azernews.az reports 11 commercial ships have been attacked in and around the strait since early October, a figure no major wire in this feed carries independently; USNI News has separately headlined "October Sees Near Daily Strikes on Ships in Hormuz." The Maritime Executive reports the IRGC has expanded its threat against vessels it deems non-compliant, and CNBC reports tanker attacks have surged to a wartime high as Iran seeks to choke off oil exports. Middle East Eye reports that CENTCOM says 133 vessels have been redirected in the Hormuz area as it enforces the Iran blockade, an unverified claim from a single source. The Canberra Times relays an Iranian claim that Iran struck a gas tanker in the strait; that claim originates with Iranian sources and carries no independent corroboration. Brent stood at $104.72 as of 15:23 UTC, up 0.83% in the last session before the close; futures markets are shut and that figure has not moved since close. On the diplomatic track, Iran has said it will respond within days to Washington's reply to its seven-day plan, whose terms have not been published, and no agreement between the two sides has been reported. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, flat over 24 hours, flagged low-confidence because two of its inputs are stale or missing (the Brent-WTI forward spread and Manifold forward contracts), with Polymarket escalation contracts as its top contributor.

Cite as
Straits, “Hormuz daily brief”, 10 Oct 2026 .
